items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to certain contracts with
out-of-state school districts
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4300

SPONSOR: CARLUCCI
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
certain contracts with out-of-state school districts

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL::


This bill extends, expands and makes permanent the provisions of Chapter
396 of the Laws of 2012 and Chapter 28 of the Laws of 2014 to allow
BOCES to contract with out-of-state schools to provide:  special educa-
tion; career and technical education services; on line courses relating
to implementation of the common cores standard; professional development
to educators; and existing technology products including computer
programs and software packages that help students learn and assist
districts in achieving greater efficiencies.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS::

  Section 1 allows BOCES to expand those services to which it is author-
ized  to  contract  with  out-of- state schools to also include existing
technology products, including computer programs and  software  packages
that help students learn and assist districts in achieving greater effi-
ciencies.  This  bill also clarifies that schools include elementary and
secondary schools as well as institutions of higher education. The  bill
further  clarifies  that  an  out-of-state school includes those located
outside of New York State, including but not limited  to  those  located
outside  of the continental United States.  Further, the bill makes this
law permanent.

  Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION::

Boards of cooperative educational services  (BOCES)  are  often  at  the
forefront of innovative and cost-saving educatidnal plans, policies, and
programs. BOCES, as innovators in the development and delivery of highly
successful  curricula, professional development for educators and proven
education programs, are already providing these programs and services to
schools in New York State. Prior to enactment of Chapter 396 of the Laws
of 2012, BOCES was not authorized to enter into contracts  with  out-of-
state  schools.  Since  this  law  was  enacted, several BOCES have, and
continue to, provide these services to schools located  outside  of  New
York.  Based  on  the  success,  the  list of those services that can be
contracted should also expanded. to include technology products and  the
law should be permanently extended.

This  law  allows  BOCES  to sell certain programs and services and as a
result generate revenue in support  of  BOCES,  their  component  school
districts  and  most importantly the students they serve.  Additionally,
to the  extent  practical,  it  enables  BOCES  to  provide  educational
services  to  out-  of  -state  students. To this end, allowing BOCES to
provide these services to out-of-state schools has been  beneficial  not
only  to the BOCES, but to New York State as a whole. For these reasons,
this law should be expanded and extended permanently.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY::

This is a new bill but it is an extension of both  Chapter  396  of  the
Laws of 2012 and Chapter 28 of the Laws of 2014.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS::

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE::

Immediately.
